title: Power-series surjection with a prescribed coefficient field and maximal-ideal generators
statement: Let $F$ be a field and let $(R,\mathfrak n)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning that $\mathfrak n$ is its unique maximal ideal, complete for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Fix a field isomorphism $\rho:R/\mathfrak n\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ and a ring homomorphism $\sigma:F\to R$ such that $\rho\circ\pi\circ\sigma=\operatorname{id}_F$, where $\pi:R\to R/\mathfrak n$ is the quotient map. Give $R$ its $F$-algebra structure through $\sigma$. For every integer $n\geq0$ and tuple $y_1,\ldots,y_n\in\mathfrak n$ generating $\mathfrak n$ as an ideal, there is a continuous surjective $F$-algebra homomorphism $\Phi:F[[T_1,\ldots,T_n]]\to R$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] with $\Phi(T_i)=y_i$ and $\Phi(c)=\sigma(c)$ for $c\in F$. Put $I=(T_1,\ldots,T_n)$. The map is continuous for the $I$-adic and $\mathfrak n$-adic topologies, $\Phi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=I$, and its kernel has a finite generating tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_s\in I$ (allowing $s=0$).

source.place: Tag 0C52 (lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra), last paragraph of the proof, with the coefficient section fixed in advance; Algebra Tag 0315 (lemma-completion-generalities) for surjectivity.

proof.text: Put $A=F[[T_1,\ldots,T_n]]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] with $\Lambda=F$, $T=R$, $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak n$, $\alpha=\sigma$ and $t_i=y_i$. Completeness and $y_i\in\mathfrak n$ are hypotheses. This gives $\Phi:A\to R$ with the required values; its agreement with $\sigma$ makes it an $F$-algebra homomorphism. Since $I$ is generated by the $T_i$ and the $y_i$ generate $\mathfrak n$, the extended ideal $I R$ through $\Phi$ is exactly $\mathfrak n$. In particular $\Phi(I^r)\subseteq\mathfrak n^r$ for every $r\geq1$, proving continuity for the stated adic topologies.

source.place: Tag 0C52 (lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra), final proof paragraph; fixed coefficient section and maximal-ideal generators

proof.text: For $g=\sum_E a_ET^E$, the degree-one congruence of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] says $\Phi(g)\equiv\sigma(a_0)\pmod{\mathfrak n}$. Hence $\rho\pi\Phi(g)=a_0$, by the fixed section identity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with base ideal $J=0$ and power $1$: it states $g\in I$ exactly when $a_0=0$. Since $\rho$ is injective, $\Phi(g)\in\mathfrak n$ exactly when $a_0=0$, so $\Phi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=I$.

source.place: Tag 0C52 (lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra), final proof paragraph; fixed coefficient section and maximal-ideal generators

proof.text: A field is Noetherian: an ideal containing a nonzero $a$ contains $a^{-1}a=1$, so every ideal is generated by either the empty tuple or $1$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Also $F$ is $0$-adically complete: all positive-power quotients are $F$ with identity transitions, so their inverse limit is $F$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-complete-over-complete-base], with $\Lambda=F$, $J=0$ and $d=n$, makes $A$ $I$-adically complete. The target is Hausdorff for $IR=\mathfrak n$ by its assumed completeness. The composite $A\to R/\mathfrak n$ is surjective: for $b\in R/\mathfrak n$ take the constant $\rho(b)$, whose image is $\pi\sigma\rho(b)=b$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-complete-source-surjective-mod-ideal] applied to $A,R,I,\Phi$ proves that $\Phi$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0315 (lemma-completion-generalities), part (1); Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), field power-series completeness

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian], applied to the Noetherian field $F$, $A$ is Noetherian. Its ideal $\ker\Phi$ therefore has a finite generating tuple by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Each chosen generator belongs to $\ker\Phi\subseteq\Phi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=I$, as required. If the kernel is zero the tuple can be empty. For $n=0$ the same argument applies with $A=F$ and $I=0$; the generator hypothesis forces $\mathfrak n=0$ and the section identity then makes $\Phi=\sigma$ an isomorphism, with empty kernel tuple.
